reader.requirement: At --std 85 UNSTRING raises the overflow condition (a) at initiation when the WITH POINTER item is less than 1 or greater than the size of identifier-1 (no transfer, pointer untouched), and (b) when all receiving areas have been acted upon while identifier-1 still holds unexamined characters, for DELIMITED (with and without ALL) and undelimited forms (size or size-minus-one for a separate sign), with GR18 then running ON OVERFLOW and skipping NOT ON OVERFLOW. Witnesses cover pointer 0/7/6/1 on size 6, two-receiver delimited and undelimited overflow and the size-0 ODO sender.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnstringZeroLengthSenderTerminates (2002 on): from 2002 a zero-length sender ends the statement before the overflow tests; at 85 the guard is absent so GR17a fires for a written pointer past a size-0 sender

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior|IsActive in StringEmitter.cs: the one IsActive site above; the GR17a/GR17b tests themselves are unconditional
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only for a zero-length (size 0 ODO) sender with a POINTER phrase, overflow at 85 versus immediate termination from 2002; every non-empty sender takes the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: not a trailing delimiter at the end of the sender, ALL-delimiter runs to the end, a remaining delimiter character after the last receiver, a negative signed pointer, a COMP pointer at size+1, separate-sign receivers examining size minus one, ON OVERFLOW with GO TO, NOT ON OVERFLOW skipped on overflow (a)

probes.printed: K1 'AB,' one receiver: NO OVERFLOW [AB ]; K2 'AB,,,' DELIMITED BY ALL: NO OVERFLOW; K3 'AB,,' not ALL: OVERFLOW [AB ] D=[, ] C=02 T=01
probes.expected: GR17b only when unexamined characters remain after the last receiver; ALL consumes the contiguous run

probes.printed: K4 pointer S99 = -1: OVERFLOW [***] P=-01; K5 COMP pointer 6 on size 6 with trailing delimiter: NO OVERFLOW [   ] P=0007; K10 pointer 6 on size 5: NOT ON OVERFLOW not run, P=0006
probes.expected: GR17a: less than 1 or greater than size is overflow at initiation, no transfer, NOT ON OVERFLOW ignored (GR18)

probes.printed: K6 '1234' INTO two S99 SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE: NO OVERFLOW 12+ 34+; K7 '12345': OVERFLOW 12+ 34+
probes.expected: GR13b separate-sign receiver examines size-1, so one character remains in K7

probes.printed: K8 undelimited X(5) INTO X(3) with POINTER 1, TALLYING: OVERFLOW [123] P=0004 T=01; K9 pointer 0 ON OVERFLOW GO TO P2: AT P2 P=0000
probes.expected: GR17b, GR15/GR16 counts kept, GR18 branch

reader.notes: EmitUnstring tests the pointer range before any transfer only when POINTER is written, then after the receivers sets overflow when the pointer is still within the sender; every probed boundary matched GR17. The only edition switch is the 2002 zero-length-sender guard, inactive at 85 as the 1985 text requires.

refuter.evidence: Read StringEmitter.cs#EmitUnstring: the GR17a test exists only with POINTER (`if (ptr < 1 || ptr > src.Length)`), GR17b is `if (ptr <= src.Length) ovf = true` after the receivers, and the only edition switch is DialectBehavior.UnstringZeroLengthSenderTerminates (2002 on). runs1-001 (--std 85): 'AB,,,C' DELIMITED BY ALL ',' INTO one receiver -> OVERFLOW [AB ] (C unexamined after the ALL run); two-character delimiter ';;' with two receivers -> NO OVERFLOW P=07; size-0 ODO sender WITH POINTER 1 -> OVERFLOW P=01 T=00 (GR17a, 1 > size 0, no transfer, tally untouched); size-0 sender without POINTER -> NO OVERFLOW (no identifier-7 to test, nothing unexamined); size 3 with pointer 4 -> OVERFLOW P=04; pointer 3 -> NO OVERFLOW P=04 [Z  ]. At --std 2023 the two size-0 statements print nothing (the 2002+ zero-length termination), the rest the same. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR17; OK §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR18.
